title: GH#37997: fix(plugin): stop runaway compaction summary loops and repair misanchored compaction boundaries
body:
## Summary

Root cause (incident session DB + OpenCode 1.19.5 source): the gpt-6-luna compaction summarizer copied a long verbatim user aim and fell into a copy loop, repeating one 91-char span (42,580 chars until the user aborted; a later attempt 9,551 chars). Only the 32K output cap bounded it. OpenCode then (a) replayed the aborted, looping summary into the next request and (b) ran the pending compaction with parentID = the user's next typed message (prompt.ts lastUser.id), which has no compaction part, so filterCompacted() skipped the boundary: the next Build+ request still sent 238,049 input tokens (32 messages, ~1.03M part chars) and triggered another compaction, which looped again.

Fix, in four small modules:

- `compaction-loop-detect.mjs` — pure tail detector and collapse.
- `compaction-history-repair.mjs` — messages.transform repair: drops failed/unfinished summaries and applies a summary anchored to a typed message as the boundary.
- `compaction-loop-recovery.mjs` — host actions: abort, rerun via session.summarize (so the new summary is correctly anchored), then continue an automatic compaction with the original agent/model/variant under the existing autocontinue policy. A `RecoveryLedger` keeps the first loop's identity for the whole rerun chain.
- `compaction-replay-collect.mjs` — the GH#35186 verbatim replay treats a typed summary parent that leads the repaired history as the boundary, so user turns trimmed before a misanchored summary are replayed.
- `compaction-loop-guard.mjs` — stream guard on message.part.delta; interactive: abort and rerun, max 2 reruns per 30 min; headless never aborted, completed summary collapsed instead. All hooks fail-open.

Opt-out `AIDEVOPS_COMPACTION_LOOP_GUARD=0`. Documented in reference/session.md.

## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-loop-detect.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-history-repair.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-loop-recovery.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-loop-guard.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-replay-collect.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-compaction-loop-guard.mjs, .agents/reference/session.md

## Decisions

Headless sessions are never aborted (opencode run would exit); they rely on the output cap plus text.complete collapse. Thresholds (2,000+ chars of one unit repeated 4+ times back-to-back) sit far above any legitimate summary repetition. Only compaction summaries are rewritten. The rerun uses the same configured compaction model; after 2 loops in 30 min the guard stops and the toast suggests /compact or pinning agent.compaction.model elsewhere. The module split keeps every new file and `AidevopsPlugin` under the Qlty complexity thresholds; `index.mjs` wiring is plain calls.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — read-only replay of the real incident session (426 messages, 11 compaction summaries) through the production guard and repair code, with a recording client in place of the host API: both looping summaries aborted at 4,714 and 4,822 streamed chars (period 91); each rerun called session.summarize with the parent turn's model (anthropic/claude-fable-5-2) and continued as Build+ with variant xhigh; the 9 clean summaries were neither aborted nor trimmed; the misanchored post-incident request was reduced from 32 messages/~1.03M part chars (238,049 recorded input tokens) to 3 messages/25,770 chars using a port of OpenCode 1.19.5 filterCompacted; on that repaired input the production verbatim replay (createCompactionInputReplay) now injects 6 parts / 5,426 chars of hidden user input, and the 8 clean boundaries are unchanged. Replay re-run after the module split and review fixes: abort points and continuations identical. Host event shape confirmed in OpenCode processor.ts (message.part.delta field text). 0 false positives across 526 clean compaction parts in the shared OpenCode DB. The production `continuation` adapter checked against the real compaction autocontinue guard (primary continues, finished child does not). tests/test-compaction-loop-guard.mjs plus compaction autocontinue tests (12 pass, including a looping rerun that keeps the original variant); the 11 index-loading suites (400 tests) pass; local `qlty smells` reports 0 smells on all changed plugin files; markdownlint clean. Live plugin load to be re-verified after release via aidevops update.

Resolves #37997

title: GH#37986: fix(pulse): bound label-maintenance starvation and re-check held issues first
body:
## Summary

Label maintenance is the only stage that removes needs-simplification and needs-consolidation holds, and it could be deferred on every cycle with no upper bound. When any substage has not started within AIDEVOPS_PULSE_LABEL_MAINTENANCE_STARVATION_S (default 7200s; 0 keeps the legacy order), the engine now runs one bounded slice (default 180s) ahead of early dispatch and skips the normal slot for that cycle. Each re-evaluation substage first re-checks the open issues that carry its label, found with one search call per group of five owners, then runs the per-repository sweep, which skips what was already re-checked and keeps at least a third of the substage time. Refill-reserve deferral lines now state remaining and required seconds.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh

## Decisions

Promotion costs early dispatch at most one 180s slice per bound and per substage. A cycle that already promoted prefetch promotes this stage only at twice the bound. A budget-deferred promoted slice leaves the normal slot free to try. A failed, incomplete or empty search never counts as proof that nothing is held: the sweep remains the safety net. The held-first step resumes after the last issue it reached, so a long held list is not re-checked from the top each run.

## Runtime Testing

- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime-verified (read-only) on a live runner: the stalest substage attempt was 249028s old and the starvation check returned starved at x1 and x2 and not-starved when disabled; the held-first search answered for 70 repos / 5 owners in about 1s and agreed with gh issue list for the checked repo. bash -n and shellcheck clean on the four changed files. test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh: 6 new assertions pass (starvation contract, held-first contract, 9l5-9l8); its 2 failures (stages clamp/defer/opt out of cycle deadline; dispatch budget admission) reproduce unchanged on the base revision. first-wave, maintenance-selector-contract, reeval-stale-continuation, simplification-auto-dispatch-backfill, consolidation-dispatch, large-file-dependency-lifecycle-canary, consolidation-multi-runner and consolidation-skip-resolved pass. title: GH#38048: fix(pulse): hand a completed full dispatch census across a cooperative bundle drain
body:
## Summary

A cooperatively drained pulse cycle (GH#37907) deleted its completed full dispatch census with the rest of its cycle cache, so the activated bundle started discovery from scratch with free slots and a ranked backlog. The drained cycle now moves the full-census snapshot and its attempt ledger to a bundle-independent handoff slot (`_dispatch_hand_off_candidate_snapshots`) while it still owns the instance lock and the drain marker exists: `_pulse_run_supervisor_phase` runs the cycle-cache cleanup before `release_instance_lock`, because the EXIT-trap cleanup only runs after the marker is gone. The activated bundle's first wave, or any bounded census, adopts the handoff as its durable snapshot (`_dispatch_adopt_candidate_handoff`) when it is inside its existing reuse window, carries the reader's snapshot schema and has a compatible normalization mode, then serves the unattempted remainder without a scan. Snapshots now carry a `schema` field. A handoff that is stale, in another format or on an unsafe path is removed unserved; an eligibility mutation invalidates an unadopted handoff with the other snapshots. The drained cycle still launches nothing, and every adopted candidate still passes the registry/schedule recheck and all live dispatch gates.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh

## Decisions

Handoff happens only under a cooperative drain, so full-census snapshots stay cycle-scoped in every other case. Only a first wave or bounded census adopts; a full round still scans for itself. The existing captured_at/census_seconds reuse window is unchanged, which means a short census can expire before the next first wave (about 6 to 13 minutes after capture in the log) and is then discarded. title: GH#38055: perf(dispatch): fetch open PR list once per footprint rebuild
body:
## Summary

The in-flight footprint rebuild now fetches the repository's open-PR list once and reuses it for every `status:claimed` issue that needs PR evidence, instead of one `gh pr list --limit 100` call per claimed issue.

Resolves #38055

## Why

Since GH#36817, every claimed issue without ledger or stamp evidence reaches Evidence 2 in `_footprint_claimed_coordinator_has_evidence`. With 22 such issues in the product repository and about 12s per `gh pr list` (56 open PRs with bodies), `dedup.footprint` averaged 93s (max 263s) per candidate and caused per-candidate stage timeouts. Parallel candidates run in separate processes, so every candidate paid the full cost.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`
  - Adds a per-rebuild memo (`_FOOTPRINT_OPEN_PRS_*`), activated and cleared by `_footprint_refresh_inflight_cache`.
  - Evidence 2 reuses the memo inside a rebuild. Outside a rebuild it always reads the live PR list, as before.
  - Evidence order and rules, the cache TTL and log lines are unchanged. A failed fetch keeps the existing "no PR evidence" semantics, now for that rebuild only rather than being retried once per claimed issue.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`
  - Test 11d: four claimed issues in one rebuild cause exactly one open-PR fetch. The issue with a `gh<N>` branch keeps its reservation, those without evidence are skipped, and the memo is cleared afterwards.

`_footprint_refresh_inflight_cache` re-parsed the whole in-flight issue JSON array 4 times per issue (number, body, parent-task flag, status:claimed flag). title: GH#38026: fix: cap the 5% free-space floor at 50 GiB and add a read-only Time Machine snapshot hint
body:
## Summary

The worktree admission gate required 5 GiB and 5% free. The 5% floor grew without bound, so a ~2 TB APFS volume needed ~100 GiB free and every worker slot idled with 80 GiB available. The percentage floor is now capped at 50 GiB (AIDEVOPS_MIN_WORKTREE_FREE_PERCENT_CEILING_KB); volumes up to 1 TB keep identical behaviour and the 5 GiB absolute floor and quota logic are unchanged. When the gate blocks on macOS, a read-only advisory names Time Machine local snapshots (whose blocks df excludes) and the owner's supported reclaim path; aidevops never thins or deletes backups. Pulse emits the hint once per process; worktree add prints it to stderr.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/throughput-throttling-policy.md, .agents/scripts/disk-capacity-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-disk-capacity-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh

## Decisions

Ceiling (not purgeable-space accounting): counting snapshot blocks as free would trust an OS reclaim promise inside a fail-closed gate. Ceiling default 50 GiB equals 5% of 1 TB so smaller volumes are unaffected. Ceiling also bounds an operator-raised percentage; raise the ceiling variable to restore pure-percentage behaviour. The 15% cleanup trigger is intentionally unchanged because cleanup reclaims rather than restricts.

## Runtime Testing

- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified on macOS (APFS, 4 real local snapshots): forced block prints the advisory, tmutil snapshot count unchanged 4->4, no hint when admission passes, default check on a 3.9 TB volume uses the 50 GiB capped floor. test-disk-capacity-lib.sh 18/18 (new rows: 2000 GiB/80 GiB admits, 2000 GiB/40 GiB blocks; existing 1000 GiB/40 GiB still blocks). test-pulse-dispatch-worktree-cap-cleanup.sh passes. shellcheck clean on all touched scripts. test-worktree-capacity-recovery.sh and test-codegraph-worktree-init-helper.sh fail identically on unmodified main (pre-existing, unrelated).

body:
## Summary

Phase 2 of the Reclaim subsystem (parent #38051). Reclaim no longer scans `/proc` to find worktree owners; it reads them from the lifecycle registry, which was built for that purpose.

- **New `reclaim/owners.py`** (read-only): opens `LifecycleRegistry` and a ready `ProcessAdapter` once per pass. For each candidate, `GenerationEnrollment.inspect_retirement` → generation runs (`cleanup_plan._runs`) → `adapter.observe` for every run not recorded as ended. Refusals: `owner-alive`, `owner-unobservable`, `owner-not-enrolled`, `owner-registry-unreadable`. If the registry or adapter is unusable, every candidate refuses with `owner-observation-unavailable`.
- **`evidence.py`**: `Census` replaced by the owner check. Order is unchanged: GitHub first, and the registry is read only for finished candidates.
- **Review-tree rule** (new `reclaim/review.py`; decision recorded in https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38107#issuecomment-6860246995). A `<repo>-pr<N>-review-<slug>` tree whose PR is confirmed `OPEN` qualifies as `review-idle` only when all of these hold: Git `HEAD`/index have been idle ≥ 2 h, no live registered owner, and `nothing_to_lose` passes (no changes, no unpushed commits). An unknown PR state still refuses. `ci-repair-prNNN` and worker trees are unaffected.
- **`host.py`**: `Census`, `process_census`, `_arguments` and `_live_same_user` are removed. `remove()` re-reads owners immediately before deletion and refuses with `owners-appeared`.
- **`sweep.py`**: adds `--state-dir`. The receipt drops `unplaceable_processes` and gains `residual_risk: unregistered-processes-unobserved` plus `owner_observation: registry|unavailable`.
- **`pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh`**: passes the state dir already resolved by `worker_lifecycle_state_dir`.
- **`.agents/reference/worktree-registry.md`**: documents the registry contract and the remaining risk.

Out of scope (later phases of #38051): decision journal/CAS, the archive stage, removal of `legacy_*`, `decide_cleanup`, `cleanup_authorized`.

title: GH#38211: perf(pulse): gate supervisor/refill/recycle on the fresh candidate census
body:
## Summary

The LLM supervisor launch (`_compute_initial_underfill`), active-pulse refill and early-exit recycle gates now use the cycle's fresh dispatch candidate census to count runnable work. Before this change they re-ran `count_runnable_candidates`, an all-repository enumeration that reconciles conversation locks and normalizes dependencies in every pulse repo. On 2026-11-14 one supervisor launch spent about 20 minutes in that count while the 20-slot pool sat at 0 workers. The delay also pushed the activated bundle's first cycle past the drain handoff's reuse window, so the 107-candidate census handed across the drain (GH#38048) was discarded as `stale_or_invalid`.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`: new `_dispatch_snapshot_runnable_count`. It is read-only and checks the cycle snapshot, the drain handoff (with a schema check) and the first-wave partial in both dependency-normalization modes. For each snapshot it applies the existing freshness rule (`_dispatch_candidate_snapshot_is_fresh` + `_dispatch_enumeration_expected_seconds`) and the consumed-attempt ledger. Cross-cycle censuses also get the first-wave registry/schedule recheck. It prints the largest unconsumed count with its source, and returns 1 when no fresh census holds candidates.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`: new `_pulse_gate_runnable_count`, which uses the snapshot count when it is positive and logs `Runnable gate (<caller>): census_snapshot count=N source=<wave>:<mode> (GH#38211)`. Otherwise it falls back to the original `count_runnable_candidates`. It replaces the four gating call sites.

Safety: these gates only decide whether to run `run_underfill_worker_recycler` / `dispatch_max`. `dispatch_max` keeps its own census and every live dispatch gate. Snapshots are never adopted, consumed or invalidated by the count. When no snapshot exists, a snapshot is stale or has a foreign schema, or snapshots are disabled (`PULSE_DISPATCH_CANDIDATE_SNAPSHOT_ENABLED=0`), the broad count still runs, so failing-PR and cold-cache behaviour does not change.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x` clean on both files; the pre-commit ratchets (returns, positional params, string literals, bash 3.2 parse) pass.
- Existing suites, all exit 0: `test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh`, `test-pulse-wrapper-worker-count.sh`, `test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh`, `test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh`, `test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh`.
- Throwaway smoke run (not committed) that sources the engine in an isolated HOME. All 7 cases pass:
  - No snapshot falls back to the broad count.
  - A cycle snapshot of 3 with 1 consumed gives 2.
  - A handoff-only census gives `1 handoff:normalize`: the registry filter drops the unknown repo and the file is left in place.
  - A foreign-schema handoff falls back.
  - An expired handoff falls back.
  - With snapshots disabled, the count falls back.
- Runtime check after deploy: the next supervisor launch logs `Runnable gate (supervisor_launch): census_snapshot ...`. The gap between `LLM supervisor: daily sweep due` / starvation-escape and `LLM supervisor attempt started` should fall from about 20 minutes to seconds.

Resolves #38211

DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=dedup_pr_evidence ... issue=#38215

title: t18987: fix(task-id-guard): name the malformed token and its source in block diagnostics (GH#38221)
body:
## Summary

When `task-id-collision-guard.sh` blocked on a malformed task identity, it reported only the sentinel (`__malformed__ — malformed task identity`). It printed the commit subject or PR title under a "Commit subject references ..." header. If the offending token was a placeholder in a commit or PR body, the report pointed at a valid subject.

Observed on PR #38218: a placeholder of the form `t` + `NNN` sat in the commit body, then in the PR body. The guard reported the valid subject. That cost two local rewrites of a valid subject plus one CI failure (`Task-ID Collision Guard`, run 43558546885).

Matching is unchanged and still fails closed. Only the diagnostics change.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/task-identity-lib.sh`: new `task_identity_first_malformed_candidate` prints the first rejected candidate. It uses the same brief-path exclusion and trailing-dot rule. `task_identity_has_malformed_candidate` is now a thin wrapper with an unchanged return contract, so `pulse-dep-graph.sh` callers are unaffected.
- `.agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh`:
  - New `_tid_scan_text` shares the claim-range scrub between `_extract_tids` and diagnostics.
  - New `_describe_malformed` names the token and its location.
  - `_check_message` takes optional location labels. Commit-msg and per-commit modes use `commit subject` / `commit body`. PR mode uses `PR title` / `PR body`. Push mode uses `commit subject` / `commit body or associated PR title/body`.
  - Header and fix hint reworded so they no longer say "Commit subject" for body or PR text. The `__malformed__` sentinel grammar is unchanged.

Example output now: `malformed task identity token '<token>' in commit body (write <task-id> for placeholders)`.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x` reports nothing on both files.
- These pass: `test-task-id-collision-guard.sh`, `test-task-id-collision-guard-reuse.sh`, `test-task-identity-lib.sh`, `test-task-brief-task-identity.sh`, `.agents/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-blocked-by.sh`, `test-pulse-dep-graph-prose-dependencies.sh`, `test-task-id-collision.sh`.
- Scratch harness, 10 cases, all pass:
  - the first-candidate token is reported
  - valid text returns rc=1
  - the `has_` wrapper works
  - trailing-dot IDs and brief paths stay valid
  - a body placeholder is blocked and named as `commit body`
  - a subject placeholder is named as `commit subject`
  - the padded legacy unpad hint is kept
  - the reworded header appears

Resolves #38221
